```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)

library(tidyverse)
library(plotly)
library(ambient)

set.seed(42)
```

## Methods

The storm surge sensitivity weight reflects joint proximity to the coast and low
elevation, such that a water supply must be *both* near the coast *and* at low
elevation to receive a high weight. A point that is close to the coast but sits
high on a bluff, or one that is low-lying but far inland, receives a lower weight
than a point that is both low and close to shore.

$$
w = \sqrt{\frac{d_{inv}^2 + e_{inv}^2}{2}}
$$

where $d_{inv} = 1 - (distance / max\_distance)$ and $e_{inv} = 1 - (elevation / max\_elevation)$,
both normalized to $[0, 1]$, and $max\_distance$ and $max\_elevation$ are the
observed maxima in the dataset.

## Terrain Generation

```{r terrain-generation}
nx <- 150
ny <- 150

x_seq <- seq(0, 1, length.out = nx)
y_seq <- seq(0, 1, length.out = ny)

# layered perlin noise: low-frequency hills, medium-frequency ridges, high-frequency roughness
base_layer  <- noise_perlin(dim = c(nx, ny), frequency = 2,  octaves = 1)
ridge_layer <- noise_perlin(dim = c(nx, ny), frequency = 6,  octaves = 1)
rough_layer <- noise_perlin(dim = c(nx, ny), frequency = 20, octaves = 1)

raw_elevation <- base_layer * 1.00 + ridge_layer * 0.35 + rough_layer * 0.10

elev_rescaled <- scales::rescale(raw_elevation, to = c(0, 400))

# coastal gradient: x = 0 (west edge) is the coast, forced low; rises inland
coast_ramp   <- x_seq^0.6
elev_coastal <- sweep(elev_rescaled, 1, coast_ramp, `*`)

# coastal bluff: sharp elevation rise near the coast within a mid-coast band
sigmoid <- function(x, center, steepness) 1 / (1 + exp(-steepness * (x - center)))

cliff_band  <- y_seq >= 0.35 & y_seq <= 0.65
cliff_boost <- sigmoid(x_seq, center = 0.15, steepness = 40) * 250

elev_final <- elev_coastal
elev_final[, cliff_band] <- sweep(elev_final[, cliff_band, drop = FALSE], 1, cliff_boost, `+`)
elev_final[elev_final < 0] <- 0

terrain_df <- expand.grid(x = x_seq, y = y_seq) %>%
  as_tibble() %>%
  mutate(elevation = as.vector(elev_final))
```

## Water Supply Points

```{r water-supply-points}
n_pts <- 20
px_seq <- seq(0, 1, length.out = n_pts)
py_seq <- seq(0, 1, length.out = n_pts)

points <- expand.grid(x = px_seq, y = py_seq) %>%
  as_tibble() %>%
  mutate(
    xi = map_dbl(x, ~ which.min(abs(x_seq - .x))),
    yi = map_dbl(y, ~ which.min(abs(y_seq - .x))),
    elevation = elev_final[cbind(xi, yi)]
  ) %>%
  select(x, y, elevation) %>%
  mutate(distance_km = x * 50)
```

## Weighting Factor

```{r weighting-factor}
max_elev <- max(points$elevation)
max_dist <- max(points$distance_km)

points <- points %>%
  mutate(
    elev_inv = 1 - (elevation / max_elev),
    dist_inv = 1 - (distance_km / max_dist),
    weight   = sqrt((dist_inv^2 + elev_inv^2) / 2),
    hover_text = paste0(
      "Elevation: ", round(elevation, 1), " m<br>",
      "Distance to coast: ", round(distance_km, 1), " km<br>",
      "Weight: ", round(weight, 3)
    )
  )
```

## 3D Visualization

```{r visualization}
# plotly surface convention: z[row, col] plots at (x[col], y[row]) -> transpose
surface_z <- t(elev_final)

fig <- plot_ly() %>%
  add_trace(
    x = x_seq, y = y_seq, z = surface_z,
    type = "surface",
    colorscale = "Earth",
    opacity = 0.85,
    hoverinfo = "none",
    showscale = TRUE,
    colorbar = list(title = "Elevation (m)", x = 1.02, y = 1, yanchor = "top", len = 0.4)
  ) %>%
  add_trace(
    data = points,
    x = ~x, y = ~y, z = ~elevation,
    type = "scatter3d",
    mode = "markers",
    marker = list(
      color = ~weight,
      colorscale = list(c(0, "green"), c(0.5, "yellow"), c(1, "red")),
      cmin = 0,
      cmax = 1,
      size = ~(4 + weight * 10),
      colorbar = list(title = "Storm Surge Weight", x = 1.02, y = 0.55, yanchor = "top", len = 0.4)
    ),
    text = ~hover_text,
    hoverinfo = "text"
  ) %>%
  layout(
    title = "Storm Surge Sensitivity Weight Explorer",
    scene = list(
      xaxis = list(title = "Distance from Coast (normalized)"),
      yaxis = list(title = "Along-coast position"),
      zaxis = list(title = "Elevation (m)"),
      camera = list(eye = list(x = 1.8, y = -1.8, z = 0.8))
    ),
    showlegend = FALSE,
    margin = list(r = 150),
    height = 700
  )

fig
```
